findings.subject: docs/known-issues-c003-wave2-r2.md:5,34-35; docs/GATES.md:1,4-10
findings.summary: The checkpoint notes still name gates v1.5 and describe C++ checking as ODR-only, while the governing design is v1.6 (a/b) and current interface coverage also includes the local shared extern-C redeclaration policy. The later notes correctly mention v1.6, so this is a nonblocking documentation inconsistency, not a missing technical fix. Repair the version/coverage wording while preserving the explicit limitation that C++ declaration types and const writes are not mechanically checked.
findings.repair: Update known-issues line 5 to v1.6 (a/b) and lines 34-35 to describe ODR plus shared-declaration policy, retaining manual type/const-write qualifications.

qualifications: All 61 required ordinary ARM functions independently MATCH: 48 new functions / 2,376 bytes and thirteen functions in twelve revised accepted units, 3,620 reviewed bytes, via sixty sequential canonical match.py commands. All 672 bound hash comparisons match, including the ten prepared project headers and both stored full-image/object/receipt bundles.

The two revised switch functions retain their published ORIGINAL BUG uninitialized out-of-range results. Revised func_00196cb8 retains the published invalid-screen before-table access after a returning error helper. Valid caller reachability/domains and arbitrary index safety remain unproven; no safe fallback was invented.

Eight required C++ units (one new and seven revised accepted; eleven total in the ledger) were manually checked against canonical headers, companion declarations/definitions and supplemental original local ABI flow. No remaining predecessor nominal declaration mismatch was found. Mechanical checks remain bounded raw-source ODR/shared-declaration scans, not a C++ parser or full type/const/namespace/alias proof.

The remaining local C++-to-C++ func_001c4500 prototype was manually compared with its definition. The textual redeclaration policy does not analyze C++ function bodies as declarations; its published limits must not be mistaken for a complete declaration/definition checker.

Partial types, reserved offsets/virtual slots, chosen names, tagged-pointer cleanup and subobject-to-owner return provenance are not unique original class identity or portable object-lifetime/storage proofs. In particular, previously opaque uses of a tag such as the pilot Widget do not establish the same complete original class as the display view. Source per-unit field/ABI consistency is reviewed, not full native class recovery.

Flexible tails remove false one-element bounds without recovering actual allocation counts. Screen/count/page/label and buffer-extent/alignment assumptions remain caller preconditions.
